questionText:

"The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) was established on 8 August 1967 in Bangkok by five visionary countries: Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand. Unlike the highly institutionalised and supranational European Union, ASEAN developed a unique form of informal, non-confrontational, and consensus-driven diplomacy known globally as the 'ASEAN Way'.
